title: Entropy Forge — a lossless compression lab
description: An interactive information-theory and data-compression laboratory, built from scratch with zero dependencies. It measures Shannon entropy (order-0/1/2) and the theoretical compression floor, then implements and visualises every major lossless codec family — a Huffman coder with a live code-tree and canonical length table; a genuine Witten–Neal–Cleary integer arithmetic coder (32-bit registers, E1/E2/E3 renormalisation, pending-bit underflow) with adaptive order-0 and order-1 models that hug the entropy bound; LZ77/LZSS sliding-window matching with a colour-coded parse map; LZW with a self-building dictionary and variable-width codes (KwKwK handled); and a full bzip2-style Burrows–Wheeler pipeline (suffix-sorted BWT with LF-mapping inverse, move-to-front, run-length, arithmetic). Composite codecs assemble the real formats — DEFLATE-lite (LZ77 tokens entropy-coded) and bzip-lite. And now THE ACTUAL FORMAT: a from-scratch, RFC 1951-compliant DEFLATE codec — the algorithm inside gzip, zlib, PNG and ZIP — with a 32 KB hash-chain + lazy-matching LZ77 stage, all three block types (stored, the canned fixed Huffman code, and a dynamic Huffman code built by the lab's own package-merge and capped at 15 bits, its length tables run-length-compressed by the 19-symbol code-length alphabet), an auto-selector that emits the cheapest block, and a puff-style inflater. It gets DEFLATE's tricky bit order exactly right (fields pack LSB-first, Huffman codes MSB-first), wraps the payload in byte-exact gzip (RFC 1952) and zlib (RFC 1950) containers with from-scratch CRC-32 and Adler-32, and — the real proof — INTEROPERATES: the .gz it emits decompresses with the browser's own gunzip, the browser's gzip inflates here, and its auto encoder matches or beats zlib level 9 on the structured corpora. A dedicated DEFLATE & gzip page shows a live native-interop badge, a stored-vs-fixed-vs-dynamic block showdown, the 32 KB LZ parse map, the full dynamic-block anatomy (HLIT/HDIST/HCLEN + the live literal/length, distance and code-length code tables), and an annotated gzip container hex dump. A Benchmark page races all codecs — real gzip included — on seven corpora against the entropy floor, every result verified by a full decode; a live Self-test round-trips every codec across the corpus plus adversarial edge cases (empty, single-symbol, all-256-bytes, long runs, pseudo-random) — 464 in-browser checks plus 28 native-gzip cross-checks — and an offline fuzz of thousands of cases (validated directly against Node's zlib) found zero mismatches.
